title: Classification of Gases
description: Oxidizers vs. inert vs. flammable gases. Compressed gases can be classified into three categories: oxidizers (contribute to combustion), inert gases (do not participate in combustion), and flammable gases (burn or explode when mixed with air/oxygen in the right concentration).

components.content:
## Gas Classification Overview

Compressed gases can be classified into three main categories:

### Oxidizers
Not flammable by themselves, but will contribute to combustion as an oxidant. Do not mix with fats or oils.

**Common oxidizers:** Air, Chlorine, Fluorine, Nitric Oxide, Nitrogen Dioxide, Oxygen

### Inert Gases
Do not take part in combustion processes and do not react with other materials. Useful for fire extinguishing systems where water damage must be avoided.

**Common inert gases:** Argon, Carbon Dioxide, Helium, Neon, Nitrogen, Xenon

### Flammable Gases
Burn or explode when mixed with air or oxygen in the right concentration range. Mixture must be within the explosive concentration limits to ignite.

**Common flammable gases:** Acetylene, Ammonia, Arsine, Butane, Carbon Monoxide, Cyclopropane, Ethane, Ethylene, Ethyl Chloride, Hydrogen, Isobutane, Methane, Methyl Chloride, Propane, Propylene, Silane
